subject.title: Feature Request: Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool)

question: Should an in-run model be allowed to request compaction of its own current session through `session_status`, under the current-session-only and fail-closed restrictions proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95272?
rationale: This creates a new model-originated session mutation that intentionally aborts and resumes a run; source inspection can assess implementation shape, but repository policy cannot decide whether that authority should be exposed.

options.title: Approve narrow self-compaction
options.body: Allow only the current live session to request compaction through the existing abort, compact, and resume lifecycle, with no cross-session capability.

options.title: Use a dedicated tool
options.body: Approve the capability but expose a separate `request_compaction` tool rather than adding a second mutation mode to `session_status`.

options.title: Keep compaction operator-controlled
options.body: Decline model-originated compaction and retain automatic, user-command, plugin-hook, and operator RPC paths only.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow self-compaction
recommendation.body: Allow only the current live session to request compaction through the existing abort, compact, and resume lifecycle, with no cross-session capability.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans the original `session_status` surface and recent gateway and compaction behavior, and this person also supplied the prior maintainer review.
